$comment: Shared conformance corpus for inbound webhook verification.
The service signs each delivery as HMAC-SHA256("<timestamp>.<rawBody>", secret) and sends
it as X-LatchVector-Signature: sha256=<lowercase hex>, with the unix seconds in
X-LatchVector-Timestamp. Both authenticity AND freshness must be checked: a signature
alone lets a captured delivery be replayed forever.
FORMAT
body              the raw body bytes, as a string. Sign and verify these exact bytes.
secret            the shared secret the receiver is configured with.
timestampOffset   seconds from now for the X-LatchVector-Timestamp header.
signature         how to build the X-LatchVector-Signature header:
"valid"            correctly computed over body+timestamp+secret
"other_secret"     correctly computed, wrong secret
"other_body"       computed over a different body
"other_timestamp"  computed over a different timestamp
{"literal": "..."}  sent verbatim
null               header absent
omitTimestamp     send no X-LatchVector-Timestamp header.
toleranceSeconds  verifier setting. Omitted means the SDK default of 300.
expect            true (accept) or false (reject).
Verification must never throw on malformed input — a webhook endpoint is reachable by
anyone who learns the URL. Every rejection here is a false return, not an exception.

vectors.name: valid
vectors.reason: The happy path.

vectors.name: valid_empty_body
vectors.reason: An empty body is still signed material. HMAC over the empty string is well defined.

vectors.name: valid_unicode_body
vectors.reason: The HMAC is over UTF-8 bytes. An SDK that decodes to a native string and re-encodes with a different codepage breaks here.

vectors.name: valid_at_tolerance_edge
vectors.reason: Just inside the 300s window. Deliveries are retried; a strict-to-the-second window would reject legitimate retries.

vectors.name: valid_clock_ahead
vectors.reason: The sender's clock may be ahead of ours. Freshness is a window around now, not a deadline in the past.

vectors.name: reject_wrong_secret
vectors.reason: Authenticity. Someone who knows the URL but not the secret.

vectors.name: reject_body_tampered_in_flight
vectors.reason: Authenticity. A valid signature for a DIFFERENT body, replayed against this one.

vectors.name: reject_timestamp_swapped
vectors.reason: The timestamp is inside the signed material precisely so it cannot be edited to refresh a captured delivery.

vectors.name: reject_replay_too_old
vectors.reason: Freshness. The signature is perfectly valid — that is the point. Without the timestamp check a delivery captured once is usable forever.

vectors.name: reject_replay_far_future
vectors.reason: Freshness in the other direction. A future timestamp is a pre-dated delivery parked for later.

vectors.name: reject_missing_signature_header
vectors.reason: No signature is not a pass.

vectors.name: reject_missing_timestamp_header
vectors.reason: Without a timestamp the freshness check cannot run, so the delivery cannot be trusted even though the bytes verify.

vectors.name: reject_empty_signature_header
vectors.reason: Input handling.

vectors.name: reject_signature_without_prefix
vectors.reason: The sha256= prefix is part of the header format. Comparing only the hex half of a header that may not have halves is how a length-confusion bug starts.

vectors.name: reject_signature_garbage
vectors.reason: Input handling. Non-hex must return false, never throw a decode exception.

vectors.name: reject_signature_truncated
vectors.reason: A short signature must fail on content, and the comparison must not read past either buffer.

vectors.name: reject_timestamp_not_a_number
vectors.reason: Input handling. An unparseable timestamp fails the freshness check rather than being treated as zero — treated as zero it would be 1970 and stale, which happens to be right, but only by accident.

vectors.name: reject_timestamp_empty
vectors.reason: Input handling. An empty string parses to 0 in several languages. It must not.

vectors.name: reject_empty_secret
vectors.reason: A misconfigured receiver with no secret must reject everything, not accept anything an attacker can compute with an empty key.

vectors.name: accept_old_delivery_when_tolerance_disabled
vectors.reason: Tolerance 0 disables the freshness check for callers who do their own replay tracking by event id. Documented, explicit, and never the default.
